analytics.title: From Calendar Chaos to Clinical Efficiency

overview.text: The Sleep and CPAP Center relied on Google Calendar to manage patient appointments, insurance information, and doctor referrals, resulting in scattered data, inefficient workflows, and difficulties tracking insurance claims. To address these challenges, I designed a custom ERP system tailored to the clinic’s operational needs. The solution centralized patient management, streamlined appointment scheduling, and enabled structured insurance claim tracking, improving administrative efficiency and reducing manual workload for staff. This project focused on transforming a fragmented process into an organized, scalable healthcare management system through user-centered design.

analytics.problem: "The Sleep and CPAP Center relied on Google Calendar to manage patient, referral, and insurance information, leading to fragmented data, inefficient workflows, and difficulty tracking insurance claims."

goal.title: Design a centralized ERP system to streamline patient management and insurance claim tracking.
goal.text:
• Centralize patient, referral, and insurance information in one system
  • Simplify appointment scheduling and management
  • Enable easy tracking of insurance claims
  • Improve workflow efficiency for clinic staff
  • Minimize data errors and information loss

onboarding.title: Designing LSE CRM around Real Users

overview.text: Lasenda, an accounting service company, faced major operational inefficiencies due to limitations of their existing CRM, Hawksoft. The system lacked essential task-tracking capabilities, making it difficult to monitor employee progress and manage workloads. Weak data encryption posed security concerns for sensitive financial information. additionally, Hawksoft provided no reliable method for handling client deadlines, increasing the risk of delays and compliance issues.

onboarding.problem: "Outdated CRM causes major inefficiency, security risks, and missed deadlines."

goal.title: Transforming workflow through secure, tailored software.
goal.text:
• Develop a secure, centralized system tailored to Lasenda's workflow.
  • Enable clear tracking of employee tasks, workloads and project progress.
  • Implement stronger data protection and encryption measures for financial information.
  • introduced automated, reliable client-deadline management to reduce missed submission.
  • Create a flexible develipment process that adapts to evolving stakeholder needs.

discover.text: To gain a deep understanding of Lasenda's operational challenges and user needs, a 5 day interview based research phase was conducted with key stakeholders and end users. These sessions focused on uncovering daily workflows, identifying pain points within the existing Hawksoft system, and understanding unmet requirements related to task management, data security and deadline handling. Insights gathered from these interviews directly informed the product requirements and helped prioritized features that would deliver the greatest impact in the LSE system.

define.text:
Background
Lasenda, an accounting services company, was experiencing operational inefficiencies due to limitations in their existing CRM system. After conducting stakeholder interviews (Super Admin, Admin, Supervisor, and Employees), I created a journey map to visualize the current workflow and uncover pain points across roles.The journey map captures the end-to-end process from client onboarding to task completion, highlighting breakdowns in task tracking, deadline management, and data security.

Key User Roles Identified

  • Customer – New or existing client 
  • Super Admin – Manages onboarding and system-level actions
  • Admin – Handles profile creation and account setup
  • Supervisor – Assigns and monitors tasks
  • Employee – Executes accounting tasks

Client Onboarding - Pain Points
  • Manual data entry
  • No structured onboarding flow
  • Difficult to manage multiple account types
  • Risk of incomplete or inconsistent information

Assign to Supervisor - Pain Points
  • No clear visibility of assignment history
  • Difficult to track supervisor workload
  • Limited progress transparency

Assign to Staff Member - Pain Points
  • Cannot assign tasks to multiple departments efficiently
  • No real-time task tracking
  • Hard to monitor progress
  • No automated notifications for new assignments

Task Completion - Pain Points
  • No structured deadline management
  • No automated reminders
  • Limited performance monitoring
  • Risk of delayed compliance submissions

Insights:

There is no centralized way to track task status, employee workload, or assignment flow. This reduces accountability and transparency.The absence of automated deadline tracking increases the risk of delays and compliance issues.Weak encryption mechanisms create risks when handling sensitive financial data.The workflow depends heavily on manual coordination between roles, increasing operational friction.

 Opportunity Areas:
  • Introduce structured onboarding forms
  • Enable task progress tracking dashboards
  • Add deadline management with automated notifications
  • Support multi-department assignment
  • Implement stronger data encryption
  • Auto-generate client IDs and agreement documents
  • Centralize relevant regulatory links

design.intro:
After clearly defining the core problems during the Define phase,  including poor task visibility, weak deadline management, and security concerns, I transitioned into the Design phase with a focused objective:To create a structured, secure, and transparent CRM experience that improves workflow efficiency across all roles. 

During this phase, I focused on:

  • Designing a clearer task assignment and tracking system
  • Improving deadline visibility with automated notifications
  • Creating structured onboarding flows
  • Strengthening data handling touch points
  • Enhancing role based dashboards for better transparency

items.text:
Problem: Users don’t know what’s pending, what’s ongoing, or what’s completed. Users struggle to identify what needs urgent attention.Updates and conversations are spread across emails, chats, and calls.Users don’t know who is responsible for what.
Solution:
  • Kanban Layout (Todo | In Progress | Completed)
  • Clear Task count indicators
  • Visual status separation using color coded sections
  • Priority Tags
  • Strong visual contrast for deadlines
  • Structured card with summaries
  • assignee avatars visible on each task
  • Centralized task based collaboration
  • Sort by newest
  • Filter by client, employee, department
  • Inline Task creation

Overall UX Impact

  • Reduces mental load
  • Improves clarity and accountability
  • Centralizes communication
  • Makes prioritization visual
  • Enables faster decision-making
Transformed task management from reactive chaos to structured, visual workflow control.

Problem:
Client onboarding often involves multiple departments, billing rules, fees, and documents — which can overwhelm users. Too many inputs on one screen can cause confusion and mistakes. Financial fields are often unclear and prone to entry errors. Uploading contracts or attachments can feel clunky. Clients may have multiple services or departments. Users worry about losing progress in long forms.
Solution:
  • Step-based vertical progress navigation (Business Info → Department Info → Payment Info → etc.)
  • Clear step indicators with numbering
  • Logical grouping of related fields
  • Section-based grouping (Department Info, Billing, Location)
  • Currency selector beside each amount
  • Payment method clearly selectable
  • Visible uploaded file confirmation
  • Modular department configuration

Overall UX Impact

  • Breaks down complexity into structured steps
  • Reduces billing errors
  • Supports scalable client setups
  • Improve data clarity
Transformed a traditionally overwhelming client setup into a guided, modular, and error-resistant experience.

Problem:
The existing invoicing system was inefficient, manual, and lacked visibility. Users struggled with inconsistent invoice creation, manual calculations, and poor payment status tracking. There was no structured workflow, no automated reminders for due dates, and limited transparency into outstanding payments.
Solution:
  • A guided, step-by-step invoice creation process was introduced to reduce errors and ensure complete data entry.
  • The system now auto-calculates totals, taxes, and service fees based on predefined rules.
  • Invoices now display real-time status indicators (Draft, Sent, Overdue, Paid).
  • Payment due dates are clearly highlighted, with automated reminders.
  • A dashboard view allows filtering by client, status, and date.

Overall UX Impact

  • Efficiency (less time spent creating and tracking invoices)
  • Accuracy (reduced billing errors)
  • Visibility (clear payment tracking)
  • Accountability (defined ownership and status clarity)
Ultimately, the redesign strengthened operational reliability while improving the overall user experience for Admins and Supervisors.

deliver.text:
After completing the Design phase, the finalized UI designs and prototypes were handed over to the development team to begin implementation. The handoff included detailed design specifications, user flows, and interaction guidelines to ensure accurate translation of design decisions into the final product. However, the process did not end at handoff. Since the project requirements evolved alongside business needs, continuous collaboration became a key part of the workflow.

Weekly Client Collaboration: Throughout development, weekly meetings were conducted with stakeholders and clients to:

  • Clarify design requirements
  • Address implementation questions
  • Validate workflows against real business processes
  • Capture requirement changes and newly identified needs
These sessions ensured alignment between design, development, and business expectations.

UX Role During Development: During this stage, my role shifted from designer to UX collaborator and design validator, where I:
  • Explained design decisions to developers
  • Updated designs based on new requirements
  • Refined user flows when business processes changed
  • Ensured usability was maintained despite scope adjustments
  • Prevented deviations from the intended user experience

Impact on the Product: Continuous UX involvement during development helped:
  • Reduce misunderstandings between stakeholders and developers
  • Adapt the system to evolving client needs
  • Maintain design consistency throughout implementation
  • Minimize rework by validating decisions early
This iterative collaboration ensured that the final product remained user-centered while accommodating real-world operational changes.
